title: Post-archive JUnit artifact recovery
outOfScope: Release/version/tag changes, archive mutation, normal PR-policy changes, and recovery paths beyond the existing bounded same-Work-Item mechanism.

sources.reason: The provider-bound recovery verifier currently reads only job logs.
The completed failed PR job has failure details in its uploaded JUnit artifact while its raw log lacks pytest failure lines.
Regression coverage for receipt validation and provider evidence binding.
The Makefile command surface is bound evidence for the generated assessment and must be refreshed with it.
Generated documentation-alignment reports must reflect refreshed bound evidence.

riskAssessment.reason: Artifact evidence can grant an append-only post-archive recovery path, so its run/job/name/download/digest/XML facts must be validated fail closed.
riskAssessment.unknownsReviewEvidence: The failed provider job and downloaded JUnit artifact establish the missing evidence channel.

reasons: Provider-bound post-archive recovery requires strict evidence integrity.

override.reason: Strict bounded correction without release operation.

executionDecision.reason: The user authorized complete cleanup and the precise provider-artifact defect is evidenced.

preReviewWarnings: Review that generic artifacts, malformed XML, mismatched run/job, and missing failures remain rejected.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: A completed failed pull-request job can use a named uploaded JUnit artifact as functional failure evidence only when the artifact is bound to the exact provider run/job and its downloaded bytes digest is recorded.
JUnit XML must contain at least one failed testcase; malformed XML, no-failure XML, missing artifact, wrong run/job, wrong SHA, success/cancelled run, and arbitrary artifacts fail closed.
The receipt preserves every existing repository, PR, candidate SHA, run/job, workflow, archive-digest, authority, and recovery-path restriction.
Focused regressions and the full governed quality route prove both the positive JUnit path and negative mutations.
guidelines: Keep recovery append-only and require source-bound provider evidence.
Do not publish releases or weaken quality, coverage, or ownership gates.

intent.problem: A real completed failed hosted PR job has canonical failure details only in its uploaded JUnit artifact. The existing log-only classifier therefore cannot prove that functional failure even though the artifact supplies precise failed pytest testcases.
constraints: Require exact GitHub repository, PR, candidate SHA, completed failed run/job, artifact identity, downloaded byte digest, and failed JUnit testcase.
Keep archives immutable and receipts append-only.
Do not release or relax quality/coverage/ownership gates.
intent.rationale: Binding the artifact through provider metadata and its content digest restores the intended recovery route without treating a cache hit or generic artifact as verification.

rawUserRequest: Continue the authorized complete cleanup and repair the real provider-bound post-archive recovery evidence gap without bypassing gates.

declaredIntent.summary: Bind a failed hosted JUnit artifact as narrow functional recovery evidence.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: The exact failed PR job exposes a JUnit artifact containing failed testcases.
scenarioCoverage.expected: A receipt records source-bound artifact evidence and may authorize only listed recovery paths.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Artifact identity, content, provider state, or JUnit failure semantics are missing or inconsistent.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Negative mutations across provider and XML artifact facts.
